content: 1. The systemic exposure of talazoparib, a substrate of the breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), may increase when co-administered with certain drugs. If co-administration cannot be avoided, monitor the patient closely for potential adverse reactions. 2. Atazanavir and tamoxifen affect the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Inhibition of CYP3A4 reduces the metabolism of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen, which has similar biological activity. Cobicistat decreases the effects of tamoxifen by interfering with CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, atazanavir increases tamsulosin levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug due to the potential for increased toxicity. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases tazemetostat levels through the same pathway. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be co-administered with tazemetostat. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of teniposide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the dosage of the P-gp substrate as recommended in its product labeling. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir and cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels of tofacitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases tofacitinib levels via the same mechanism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Cobicistat also increases tolvaptan levels via the same pathway, and co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of toremifene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day prior to the next infusion. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Atazanavir increases the levels of triazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid using tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat also increases vemurafenib levels via the same pathway. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate (inhaled) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Cobicistat also increases vilazodone levels via the same pathway. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Vonoprazan decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases vorapaxar levels via the same pathway. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases voriconazole levels via the same pathway. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Atazanavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase the abemaciclib dose after 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor to the pre-inhibitor dose. 29. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Atazanavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. New-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. 32. Atazanavir increases the effects of acebutolol through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 33. Atazanavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 34. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when co-administered with antiarrhythmics. 37. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases amitriptyline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Atazanavir increases the levels of amoxapine through an unspecified mechanism. Cobicistat also increases amoxapine levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also increases apalutamide levels via the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apixaban by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases aripiprazole levels via the same pathway. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25%, and by approximately 50% if co-administered with both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibitors. 44. Atazanavir increases the levels of artemether by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. Use alternatives if available. 45. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via the same pathway. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Atazanavir increases the effects of atenolol through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat also increases atorvastatin levels via the same pathway. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of avatrombopag by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. When treating immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), co-administration with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors requires a decreased avatrombopag starting dose. Refer to the drug monograph for specific recommendations. 50. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 51. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Belzutifan also decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir via the same pathway. If co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate dose according to its prescribing information. 52. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone (the active metabolite of benzhydrocodone) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Atazanavir also increases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels via the same pathway.
